english: Calling upon the aid of the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the one true God,
we begin to write {OCR? ܡܦܲܓ݂ܪܵܦܘܼ: transcribe/write} the Book of Chronography
composed by Mar Gregory, Maphrian,
light of the East and the West,
who is Abu'l-Faraj, son of Aaron the physician, from the city {OCR? ܕܝܼܢ̄ܬܵܐ for ܡܕܝܼܢ̄ܬܵܐ} of Melitene,
and surnamed Barhebraeus.
First, the Introduction.
O God, help my weakness.
Blessed are You, Lord and Master of every beginning and completion {OCR? or dissolution};
You are the first and You are the last.
And toward You every course is directed,
and to You all thanksgiving is owed,
and to the Son, the Word, the power of Your wisdom,
and to the Holy Spirit, the life of Your essence,
from eternity, and now, and forever.
And because this rational animal was created to know righteousness in order to praise it, and the good in order to find it,
and attains to that former knowledge through theoretical thoughts,
and to this second through practical reports {OCR? or experiences},
the commemoration of events, therefore, both good and bad, which have been performed in every generation,
bestows no small benefit upon all those who are eager to acquire the good
and diligent to hate the evil,
inasmuch as it incites one to search out {OCR? or emulate} the virtues of the former,
and urges one to cast away the vices of the latter.
